methodological_rigor.justification: This retrospective study develops an attention-based multiple instance learning pipeline to predict four cytogenetic markers from bone marrow aspirate smears using patient-level FISH labels, with patient-level stratified splitting into train/validation/test sets (60/20/20) to prevent leakage. The cohort is reasonably sized for this setting (720 patients; 3,240 digitized smears with quality control; 182,943 plasma cells), and the workflow includes explicit slide exclusion criteria (e.g., plasma cell content <10% and artifact burden >20%). Key limitations remain: the cohort is from a single institution and the paper itself contains some inconsistent framing (e.g., abstract calling it multi-center while Methods describe a single-site cohort in 2025), and there is no external or prospective validation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The clinical objective is directly relevant to MM management because it targets high-risk markers such as del(17p), t(4;14), and gain(1q), and the therapeutically actionable t(11;14) subgroup, using routinely prepared smears paired with standard FISH testing. Reported discrimination on the held-out test set is moderate-to-good (AUCs 0.76–0.85 across markers; e.g., t(11;14) AUC 0.85 and del(17p) AUC 0.82 with confidence intervals), supporting potential use as a screening or triage tool. However, the manuscript acknowledges the need for prospective validation before deployment, so the findings should not be treated as practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: The Methods provide substantial technical detail on staining, scanning, quality control, segmentation, feature extraction (DinoBloom embeddings), and evaluation (ROC curves with confidence intervals and DeLong tests; Bonferroni correction in subgroup/feature analyses). At the same time, reporting does not read as explicitly checklist-driven for diagnostic accuracy (no STARD-style flow diagram/checklist items are signposted, and external validation is absent). The manuscript does not include a clear data/code availability statement in the provided text, which limits reproducibility despite detailed descriptions.

novelty_literature.justification: The work positions itself as combining a hematology-specific foundation model (DinoBloom), attention-based MIL, and multi-task prediction to infer multiple MM cytogenetic markers from cytology smears, rather than tissue biopsies. It also provides interpretability via attention heatmaps and attempts biological plausibility checks (e.g., attention patterns aligning with known morphology-genetics associations such as mature lymphoplasmacytoid features for t(11;14)). While morphology-genetics correlations in MM are known and prior AI work exists in hematologic smear genetics, the specific multi-marker, weakly supervised cytology approach is a meaningful extension.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally well organized with a clear description of the end-to-end pipeline and concrete performance summaries (AUCs, sensitivities/specificities, and comparative baselines). Figures and tables are referenced to support cohort structure, test-set performance, and explainability outputs. Minor clarity issues remain, including inconsistent characterization of the cohort (multi-center vs single-center language) and some dense, highly technical passages that could be tightened for clinical readers.

key_strengths: Large retrospective dataset with patient-level splitting (720 patients; 182,943 plasma cells) and explicit smear quality-control/exclusion criteria.
Clinically motivated targets (del(17p), t(4;14), gain(1q), t(11;14)) with moderate-to-good held-out test discrimination (AUC ~0.76–0.85) and confidence intervals.
Interpretable attention-based MIL framework, including attention heatmaps and morphology-genetics plausibility checks.
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with no external or prospective validation, limiting generalizability across stains/scanners and clinical workflows.
Inconsistent description of cohort provenance within the manuscript (abstract suggests multi-center, while Methods describe a single-institution cohort), which needs clarification.
No clear data/code availability statement in the provided text, reducing reproducibility and independent verification.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a solid translational computational pathology study with a coherent pipeline and encouraging internal test-set performance, but the lack of external validation and some internal reporting inconsistencies make it better suited to a mid-tier oncology journal after major revisions and clarification.
